subject: Is there a use parameter posterior from old analysis as prior in new analysis?

messages.author: 9febcbf26d2ccc5b
messages.subject: Is there a use parameter posterior from old analysis as prior in new analysis?
parts:
Normally within the model block I might specify a prior on a parameter with 

    y ~ normal(mu, sigma);

But what if I already have a posterior on y from a previous analysis, and what to use that posterior as the prior in the new analysis.  Can I import a set of samples from the old posterior and sample from that?   How is that done?  Can I import an entire Stan object from an old analysis and use the parameter distributions coded therein?

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Is there a use parameter posterior from old analysis as prior in new analysis?
parts:
You can't do this in any direct way, as Stan does not have particle filters.  The most direct approach would be to include your old data and prior (which you used to construct your posterior) and your new data into a single model and perform Stan on all of it at once.  If you really want to first do inference and then take those simulations as a prior, I suppose you could approximate those simulations in some parametric form such as multivariate normal or mixture of multivariate normals, then use this parametric approx as your prior.
A

P.S.  In our usual notation, y would be data, not a parameter!  We usually label data as x,y, etc., and label parameters as alpha, beta, etc and a, b, etc.

parts:
Hi Dr. Gelman

Thanks so much for your help.  I did what you suggest and still have some issues.  I am working on an interesting systems biology ODE problem, which I think could turn into a useful R Stan tutorial on the subject.

I have some of the code here in vignette form.  

https://github.com/robertness/signalnet/blob/master/R%20package/vignettes/Raf_ss_ts_model.Rmd

Is there any chance I could talk with someone in your group about my implementation?  

Specifically, I wrote a model for inference of two rate parameters "a" and "b"  in an ODE.  I have data from two times of experimental platforms, one that collects multivariate steady state single time point measurements cheaply, and one that collects expensive time course measurements of only a few variables.  My idea is to do inference with steady state measurements, and then use this to improve the inference in time course data collected from a subsequent experiment.  I eventually hope to build this into an experimental design approach.  One caveat, a and b are not identifiable from the steady state data but w = a/b is.     

Regards,
Robert

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Is there a use parameter posterior from old analysis as prior in new analysis?
parts:
You are on the right list for questions about Stan.
Most of our systems biology ODE experts are outside of
Columbia but are on our mailing list. The list is high
volume, so if you're interested in ODEs, I'd start a new
thread with that in the title.

We always welcome case studies:

http://mc-stan.org/documentation/case-studies.html

Multiplicatively non-identifiability is highly problematic as
it leads to banana-shaped posteriors that defeat our adaptation
(no fixed mass matrix is appropriate throughout the posterior).
But if that's only one of the data sets, it should be OK as it's
still providing some information constraining the relation between
a and b.

If the two data collection processes share parameters, then it
is straightforward to write the Bayesian model to handle both
jointly---just include both sets of data and model the joint
likelihood of that data and provide a single set of priors on
the parameters.

We are about to introduce a matrix exponential function specifically
for handling some steady-state computations in ODEs. I'm hoping
it'll be ready for our 2.13 release later this year. If not, it'll
be in 2.14.

- Bob
